name: Polska

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.persona: A seasoned Nordic folk dancer with deep knowledge of regional Swedish and Norwegian styles.
instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Danced primarily as a couple, featuring walking promenades, counter-clockwise upper-body turns (bakmes), and rapid clockwise rotations (pols) executed in triple time.
Watch for Bakmes turn, Pols turn.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (lRl1T7CAD0E)
Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Couples traveling counter-clockwise around the periphery of the floor or stationary on a spot
scenes.music: diegetic (the video's own sound), underscore under narration

scenes.title: Listen
narration: Played on standard violins and the Hardanger fiddle, structured around repeating 32 or 64-measure phrases with variable rhythmic accents.
Listen for the standard fiddles (violins), hardingfele (Hardanger fiddle).
The pulse is 3/4 time (with 2/4 and compound variations).
Fiddles drive the melody through repeating motifs, drone strings on the Hardanger fiddle, and uneven beats where musicians traditionally tap only the first and third beats.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Archivists and researchers such as those from Svenskt visarkiv and regional contributors who documented disappearing traditions in the mid-20th century.
Includes Norwegian pols and springar, Swedish slängpolskas in Småland, and diverse community styles across Dalarna and Uppland.
Descended from 17th-century European court dances and Nordic folk songs; gave rise to modern forms like the Swedish hambo.
on_screen: Names on screen as they are spoken
Variant names as a small list

scenes.title: Family tree
narration: Polska is parent of Polonaise: Early court inspiration from 17th-century Poland.
Polska is child of Hambo: Swedish national dance derived from the polska tradition.
Polska is variant of Springar: Norwegian mountain variant featuring asymmetrical triple time.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Polska (Sweden). Meter 3/4 time (with 2/4 and compound variations). Form: Two or three eight-bar phrases, each repeated (32 to 64 measures per tune cycle). Mood: energetic, dizzying, lyrical, asymmetrical.
